test_title: PYST 14: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I - GA (Held On: 11 Jun, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: According to the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) report, what was the Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR) for women in 2021-22?
solution:
The correct answer is __**32.8%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR) for women in India in 2021-22 was **32.8%**, according to the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) report.
 
• LFPR is defined as the percentage of persons in the labor force (employed or seeking employment) in the population aged 15 years and above.
 
• The increase in LFPR for women in recent years reflects the government's initiatives to improve gender participation in the workforce.
 
• The PLFS report is a flagship survey conducted annually by the **National Statistical Office (NSO)** to provide estimates of key employment and unemployment indicators.
 
• India's overall LFPR (including men and women) in 2021-22 was also reported to have improved compared to previous years.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS):**

 
 
• PLFS was launched by the NSO in **2017** to provide employment and unemployment data on a quarterly and annual basis.
 
• The survey provides insights into key labor market indicators such as LFPR, Worker Population Ratio (WPR), and Unemployment Rate (UR).
 
 
 
• **Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR):**
 
 
• LFPR is an important measure of the active workforce in an economy.
 
• It includes people aged 15 and above who are either employed or actively seeking employment.
 
• A higher LFPR indicates a higher proportion of the population is economically active.
 
 
 
• **Factors Influencing Female LFPR:**
 
 
• Socio-cultural norms and family responsibilities often influence women's participation in the workforce in India.
 
• Government initiatives like Skill India, Stand-Up India, and increased opportunities in the informal sector have positively impacted female LFPR.
 
 
 
• **Government Initiatives to Boost Female Participation:**
 
 
• Programs like **Mahila Shakti Kendra** and **Beti Bachao Beti Padhao** aim to empower women and enhance their participation in various sectors.
 
• Legislation like the Maternity Benefit (Amendment) Act, 2017 provides support for working mothers, encouraging women to stay in the workforce.
